stories.title: Cerebras separates prompt processing from token generation
stories.alt: Conceptual diagram showing AMD GPU prompt prefill, transfer of model state, and Cerebras CS-3 token decoding.
stories.facts: Cerebras describes a production deployment using AMD Instinct GPUs for prompt processing and CS-3 systems for output generation. It reports five times the throughput per megawatt versus its CS-3-only configuration on a shared GPT-OSS-120B endpoint measured November 14.
stories.inference: Why it matters: benchmark end-to-end latency and throughput separately. For research assistants, faster inference can reduce iteration time; it does not establish better forecasting skill.
stories.uncertainty: Vendor-reported, workload-specific performance; no independent replication established here.

stories.title: Audit of 91 LLM trading papers flags weak cost and leakage controls
stories.alt: Evidence-screening diagram with transaction costs, chronological validity, and trial-count disclosure as three separate checks.
stories.facts: A preregistered audit reports that 51% of 75 papers with trading tests deduct no trading costs; only 9% model costs from data. The median test window is 12 months. Only five papers combine deducted costs, a leakage control and a reported trial count.
stories.inference: Why it matters: require those three disclosures before treating an LLM strategy result as candidate evidence. Reproduce net performance with point-in-time inputs before comparing models.
stories.uncertainty: Preprint findings depend on the selected corpus and coding rubric; this is not a replication of every trading strategy.

stories.title: Nasdaq futures rebound in a reported premarket snapshot
stories.alt: Bar chart of reported futures changes: Dow plus 0.11 percent, S&P 500 plus 0.41 percent, Nasdaq 100 plus 0.90 percent at 6:47 a.m. EST.
stories.facts: Reuters reported Dow E-mini futures up 0.11%, S&P 500 E-minis up 0.41% and Nasdaq 100 E-minis up 0.90% at 6:47 a.m. EST (5:47 a.m. CST), following Nvidia’s forecast.
stories.inference: Why it matters: a technology-led rebound can widen QQQ versus SPY exposure differences. Verify auction imbalances and executable quotes before treating the gap as a tradable continuation signal.
stories.uncertainty: Reported snapshot, not live quotes. Futures direction does not measure spreads, order-book depth or opening fills.

stories.title: October FOMC minutes are due at 1 p.m. Central
stories.alt: Event-clock diagram showing the October 27–28 meeting, November 18 minutes release at 1 p.m. CST, and subsequent execution-risk reassessment.
stories.facts: The Federal Reserve’s calendar schedules minutes of the October 27–28 meeting for November 18 at 2 p.m. EST, equivalent to 1 p.m. CST.
stories.inference: Why it matters: treat the release as a scheduled liquidity and repricing event. Reassess spreads and short-dated options exposure around the release rather than predicting the contents.
stories.uncertainty: Minutes were not released at this research cutoff. They describe the earlier meeting and do not constitute a new rate decision.

stories.title: Lowe’s sales grow, while tariff refunds complicate earnings comparisons
stories.alt: Three-box earnings panel showing Lowe’s 1.8 percent comparable-sales growth, 3.10 adjusted diluted EPS, and 0.34 tariff-refund benefit included in EPS.
stories.facts: Lowe’s reported sales of $22.8 billion, up 9.3%, and comparable-sales growth of 1.8%. Adjusted diluted EPS was $3.10; both GAAP and adjusted EPS include a $0.34 benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds. Its earnings call is scheduled for 9 a.m. EST today.
stories.inference: Why it matters: separate recurring demand, acquisitions and refund effects when updating earnings features. Headline adjusted EPS is not a clean measure of recurring operating improvement.
stories.uncertainty: Company-reported unaudited results; guidance remains forward-looking. This briefing does not infer a share-price reaction.
